method: Separate public source searches in new reader sessions received only the issuer and independently identified numerical target. Both sides had to substantiate the date, consolidated whole-range guidance or actuals, category and prior disclosure coverage. A null or differing date stays explicit. Source-window coverage still depends on the available issuer archive.

independent_review.basis: ADM’s July 25 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its Consolidated Statements of Earnings reported revenue of $25,190 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2023, versus $27,284 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2022. That was a 7.675% decline, placing Q2 revenue $729.8 million below the $25,919.8 million threshold. Both figures come from the same consolidated GAAP revenue row.

coverage.detail: January 26, Q4 2022 release. ADM reported December-quarter results and discussed its positioning for 2023 without giving a Q2 2023 consolidated revenue forecast.
January 26 earnings call. Management’s 2023 planning assumptions included at least 10% constant-currency operating-profit growth in Nutrition. The call gave no Q2 consolidated sales ceiling.
March 1 Bank of America conference. The Ag Services & Oilseeds president discussed throughput, crush capacity and margins without quantifying ADM’s Q2 consolidated revenue.
April 3 Form 8-K. The $500 million figure was the principal amount of a notes offering.
April 25, Q1 2023 release. The actuals covered the quarter ended March 31. Forward comments addressed margins and Nutrition earnings growth without giving a Q2 consolidated revenue range.
The Q1 earnings presentation showed quarterly operating profit by segment and historical Nutrition revenue. It supplied no Q2 consolidated sales ceiling.
April 25 earnings call. Management explicitly expected Q2 crushing results and ethanol margins to be lower year over year. Neither statement quantified Q2 consolidated revenue.
May 8 Form 8-K, the only intervening 8-K between the Q1 and Q2 earnings releases. It reported voting results from the May 4 annual meeting.
May 17 BMO conference. The CFO reiterated a $6 to $7 EPS range for full-year 2023. The remarks gave no Q2 consolidated sales range.
May 31 Bernstein conference. The CEO’s approximately $100 billion revenue figure described ADM’s overall scale. He gave no Q2 consolidated revenue estimate.
July 12 notice. ADM scheduled Q2 results for July 25 before market open and supplied no preliminary figures.
July 25 Form 8-K identifies Exhibit 99.1 as ADM’s press release dated July 25 announcing second-quarter results.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: ADM’s investor-relations release is dated July 25, 2023 and states that ADM reported results that day for the quarter ended June 30. The July 12 advance notice and the July 25 Form 8-K independently corroborate the release date.

independent_review.basis: ADM’s fourth-quarter results release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its Consolidated Statements of Earnings report revenue of $18,556 million for the quarter ended December 31, 2025, versus $21,498 million for the corresponding 2024 quarter. The 13.685% decline puts reported revenue below the $20,423.1 million cutoff. Both figures come directly from the same quarterly GAAP table and include Other Business.

coverage.detail: August 5, 2025, Q2 release. ADM guided to approximately $4.00 in full-year adjusted EPS and expected improved margins to benefit Q4. It gave no consolidated Q4 revenue range.
August 5 call. Management projected Q4 global crush margins of $60–$70 per metric ton for soybeans and $55–$65 for canola. Neither per-ton measure establishes companywide sales.
September 3 Barclays conference. Management discussed Q4 processing capacity, crop availability, ethanol margins and Nutrition plant utilization. It gave no numeric consolidated Q4 revenue outlook.
September 23 Alltech announcement. ADM expected the animal-feed venture to launch in Q1 2026. The announcement supplied no revised consolidated Q4 2025 sales figure.
November 4 Q3 release. ADM reduced full-year adjusted EPS guidance from approximately $4.00 to $3.25–$3.50. It supplied no annual revenue forecast from which to infer Q4 sales.
November 4 presentation, slide 10. ADM revised Q4’s expected share of second-half adjusted EPS from approximately 65% to 40%–50%. The percentages describe the timing of earnings.

November 4 call. The CFO projected a roughly 10% year-over-year decline in Q4 ethanol EBITDA margins and quantified expected insurance proceeds by segment. Neither disclosure bounded consolidated Q4 revenue.

December 3 Goldman Sachs conference. Management discussed export demand and crush margins. The cited revenue record concerned Q3 North American Flavors sales. Management gave no consolidated Q4 sales estimate.
December 18 Planters announcement. The parties expected the cottonseed venture to close and launch in Q1 2026. The announcement gave no consolidated Q4 sales update.
January 12, 2026. ADM scheduled the February 3 earnings call and said a results release would precede it. The notice contained no preliminary sales figure.
January 27 release, furnished with the January 28 Form 8-K. ADM disclosed a $40 million settlement over historical intersegment sales reporting. It gave no Q4 consolidated revenue figure.

February 3 results release. The quarterly revenue breakdown reconciles $18,439 million of segment revenue plus $117 million of Other Business to $18,556 million. The comparable 2024 amounts were $21,398 million plus $100 million, totaling $21,498 million.
EDGAR accepted the Item 2.02 Form 8-K containing the results release as Exhibit 99.1 on February 3, 2026, at 06:03:39 ET.

independent_review.basis: The July 1 earnings release was the earliest qualifying communication. For Q1 FY2026, the three months ended May 31, 2025, the GAAP table reports consolidated net sales of $2,515.0 million versus $2,661.8 million a year earlier. coverage.detail: January 10, Q3 FY2025 release and call. The company lowered its outlook for the fiscal year ending February 28, 2025. Its enterprise organic net sales growth range was 2% to 5%. Management gave no consolidated sales ceiling for Q1 FY2026.

April 9, Q4 FY2025 release. The FY2026 outlook called for enterprise organic net sales growth of −2% to +1%, beer net sales growth of 0% to 3%, and a wine and spirits organic net sales decline of 17% to 20%. All three ranges covered the full year.

April 10 earnings call. Asked specifically about Q1, CEO Bill Newlands said the prior-year quarter was the strongest comparison and that the company generally did not issue quarterly guidance. He gave no numeric Q1 consolidated sales range.

April 23 Form 10-K. Management expected depletion volume to outpace shipment volume most notably in Q1. That statement about volume provided no dollar or percentage ceiling for consolidated net sales.

May 13 Goldman Sachs forum. Asked about March through May beer shipments, management declined to give quarterly or monthly figures. The 6.4% growth figure cited referred to the prior-year beer comparison.
June 2 wine transaction announcement. The sale closed after the May 31 quarter end. The company reaffirmed its April fiscal-year outlook and supplied no preliminary Q1 consolidated sales figure.
June 3 Deutsche Bank conference. The CEO and CFO discussed consumer demand, FY2026 guidance, beer margins and the wine sale. Their remarks gave no numeric Q1 consolidated sales result or upper bound.

The IR archive timestamps the Q1 results release at 4:05 p.m. EDT on July 1. Its May 29 notice scheduled the release, and its June 2 announcements concerned the wine closing and debt redemption. The archive shows no intervening preliminary earnings release.

July 1 Exhibit 99.1 reconciles the revenue bases. Prior-year reported sales included $36.0 million from SVEDKA. Removing that amount gives the $2,625.8 million organic comparison and a rounded 4% decline. The reported comparison retains SVEDKA and yields the qualifying 5.52% decline.
The July 2 Form 10-Q confirms the same consolidated net sales amounts and the $146.8 million year-over-year decrease.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Exhibit 99.1 is dated July 1, 2025. The issuer’s timestamped IR announcement confirms publication that day at 4:05 p.m. EDT, before the July 2 earnings call and Form 10-Q.

coverage.detail: February 6, 2023. The preceding earnings release gave a $467 million ±3% revenue outlook for Q1 2023. Its outlook covered the quarter ending March 31.
The February 6 management call likewise identified Q1 as the forecast period. I found no numeric Q2 sales ceiling in the transcript.

On the May 9 public earnings call, management repeated the $467 million ±3% Q2 forecast. The discussion of June-quarter inventory reductions supplied no tighter consolidated sales ceiling.

Diodes’ May 17 announcement listed Mizuho on May 31, a publicly webcast TD Cowen fireside chat on June 1, and a Baird fireside chat on June 6. The announcement contained no revised forecast. I could not verify a recording or transcript of the June 1 remarks.
Diodes’ event page confirms the June 6 Baird chat and states that the webcast is unavailable. I could not verify its remarks from a primary transcript.
Diodes’ July 18 notice scheduled the August 8 Q2 results release and conference call. It gave no preliminary sales figure or revised range.

August 8, 2023. The consolidated statements of operations report net sales in thousands of dollars of 467,152 and 500,972 for the three months ended June 30, 2023 and 2022, respectively. Both figures come from the same reported net sales row.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Diodes’ Q2 results release is datelined August 8, 2023 in Plano, Texas and says the company reported its June-quarter results that day. This establishes the publication date of the verified actuals. The June conference remarks remain the gap in establishing the earliest qualifying public date.

independent_review.basis: Dine Brands publicly established the threshold by March 1, 2023. Its consolidated income statement reports Q4 FY2022 total revenue of $207,965,000 against $229,630,000 in Q4 FY2021. That is a 9.43% decline and $10,183,500 below the $218,148,500 cutoff. I found no earlier qualifying figure in the disclosures reviewed. The earliest date remains unverified because I could not check the complete November 2 call or the issuer’s historical events archive for the intervening period.

coverage.detail: August 9, 2022, preceding earnings cycle. The Q2 release reaffirmed fiscal-year guidance for restaurant openings and closures, adjusted EBITDA, G&A and capital expenditures. It gave no Q4 consolidated revenue ceiling. On the accompanying call, management likewise described its outlook as full-year guidance.

November 2, 2022, Q3 earnings release, Exhibit 99.1. The updated $243 million to $248 million range was full-year adjusted EBITDA. It incorporated planned Q4 spending and the Applebee’s refranchising. The guidance contained no full-year or Q4 consolidated revenue range from which to calculate a revenue ceiling. The release identifies the same-day call and says its replay would be available for a limited time.

November 2 call, secondary transcript evidence. Indexed management remarks linked the remaining quarter’s outlook to G&A spending and refranchising. The available excerpts supplied no numeric Q4 total-revenue bound. I could not verify the complete call, including Q&A.

December 5, 2022, Fuzzy’s acquisition announcement. The approximately $230 million forecast covered Fuzzy’s full-year systemwide restaurant sales. It supplied no Q4 consolidated revenue bound for Dine Brands.

December 5 acquisition presentation, Exhibit 99.2. The $80 million figure was the cash purchase price. The deck discussed expected earnings accretion and brand economics without stating a Q4 consolidated revenue ceiling.

February 15, 2023. An indexed wire copy of the issuer’s scheduling notice said Dine Brands would announce Q4 results March 1 before the market opened. The available notice excerpt gave no preliminary revenue figure.

March 1 actual results, Exhibit 99.1. The quarterly total-revenues row gives 207,965 and 229,630 in thousands of dollars. Both figures use the issuer’s reported consolidated perimeter. Dine Brands attributed the decline primarily to its October sale of 69 company-operated Applebee’s restaurants. Fuzzy’s joined the group in December.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: The issuer’s release is dated March 1, 2023 and says it announced Q4 and fiscal 2022 results that day. Item 2.02 of its [Form 8-K](https://investors.dinebrands.com/static-files/9787f274-0765-461d-98ed-7dfa56eaafc5) independently confirms the release was issued March 1. The numeric upper bound is the verified actual from that release.

independent_review.basis: Kennametal’s May 7 earnings release was the earliest qualifying public disclosure found. Its consolidated income statement reports fiscal Q3 2025 sales of $486,399,000 against $515,794,000 for the three months ended March 31, 2024, a 5.70% decline. The February guidance midpoint of $490,000,000 fell just below the $490,004,300 cutoff, but the explicit upper bound was $500,000,000.

coverage.detail: November 6, 2024. The $480–500 million quarterly sales outlook applied to fiscal Q2, ending in December. The $2.0–2.1 billion outlook covered the full fiscal year. Neither established a March-quarter upper bound.
February 5, 2025. The Q2 earnings release explicitly forecast fiscal Q3 sales of $480–500 million, including the expected currency headwind. The high end exceeded the cutoff by $9,995,700.
The February 5 earnings-call presentation, slide 10, confirms the $480–500 million Q3 sales range. The separate decline of 6% to 2% refers to volume. The CFO repeated the dollar range on the call.
The January 29 notice announced management attendance at Barclays on February 19. It gave no Q3 sales figure or public webcast details.
The February 21 notice announced management attendance at J.P. Morgan on March 12. It gave no Q3 sales figure or public webcast details.

Kennametal’s public webcast and presentation archive lists the February 5 and May 7 earnings calls consecutively. The search found no intervening public presentation, management remarks, or preliminary release with a revised numeric Q3 sales ceiling.
April 16. Kennametal scheduled its Q3 earnings call and said the release and presentation would be available before market on May 7. The notice gave no preliminary sales figure.
The April 30 Form 8-K disclosed a $0.20 quarterly dividend and gave no Q3 sales update.
The May 1 Form 8-K concerned board membership and gave no Q3 sales update.

May 7. The consolidated sales row, in thousands of dollars, shows 486,399 and 515,794 in the respective March-quarter columns. Both totals include Metal Cutting and Infrastructure. Management described sales as slightly below its outlook midpoint.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Kennametal’s investor-relations release carries a May 7, 2025 Pittsburgh dateline and states that it reported results that day. The same release appears as Exhibit 99.1 to the earnings Form 8-K.

independent_review.basis: May 31, 2023 is the earliest qualifying disclosure I could verify. Nordstrom reported consolidated Q1 FY2023 total revenue of $3.181 billion, down 10.87% from $3.569 billion and below the $3.39055 billion cutoff. The earliest-date verdict remains open because Nordstrom’s separately archived March 2 investor slides could not be read. The March 2 release, prepared remarks and call transcript supplied no explicit Q1 revenue ceiling.

coverage.detail: November 22, 2022, Q3 FY2022 earnings release and 8-K. The 5% to 7% consolidated revenue growth outlook applied to FY2022, which ended January 28, 2023, before the target quarter began.
December 6 Morgan Stanley conference. Management discussed Q4 holiday volume and its inventory strategy entering 2023. I found no numeric Q1 FY2023 consolidated revenue bound.
January 19 holiday update. The 3.5% net sales decline covered the nine weeks ended December 31, 2022. The revised outlook covered FY2022.

March 2 Q4 FY2022 release. Nordstrom forecast a 4% to 6% FY2023 revenue decline, including the Canadian wind-down and the 53rd week. The range's high end was 96% of prior-year annual revenue. It supplied no Q1 revenue ceiling.

March 2 earnings call, including Q&A. Management expected a low-double-digit revenue decline for the first half. The 19% Q1 growth figure referred to the prior year's performance. The Q1 breakeven estimate concerned EBIT.
The issuer separately lists Q4 FY2022 slides, prepared remarks and a transcript. The slide download returned HTTP 403, leaving its standalone contents unverified.
April 17 interim 8-K exhibit announced Eric Sprunk’s board appointment and gave no quarterly revenue update.
The April 28 proxy scheduled the annual shareholder meeting for June 6, after the Q1 earnings release.
The May 10 disclosure concerned Cathy Smith’s appointment as CFO and gave no Q1 revenue estimate.
May 11 notice scheduled the results for May 31 after market close. It contained no preliminary results or guidance figures.

May 31 actuals. The consolidated earnings table gives $3,064 million in net sales plus $117 million in net credit card revenue for the quarter ended April 29, 2023. The April 30, 2022 comparative gives $3,467 million plus $102 million. The reported totals include Canada through March 2 in FY2023 and for the full prior-year quarter.
EDGAR records acceptance of the 8-K containing the earnings release as Exhibit 99.1 on May 31, 2023 at 16:34:56.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Nordstrom dated the qualifying actual-results release May 31, 2023, and EDGAR accepted it that afternoon. The dollar bound is the actual published on that date. The June 7 Form 10-Q followed the release.

independent_review.basis: Rite Aid’s June 29 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its consolidated statement of operations reported revenue of $5,653,162,000 for the 13 weeks ended June 3, 2023 (Q1 FY2024), compared with $6,014,583,000 for the 13 weeks ended May 28, 2022 (Q1 FY2023). Revenue declined 6.0091% and was $60,691,850 below the $5,713,853,850 threshold. The upper bound is the reported actual.

coverage.detail: December 21, 2022, preceding earnings cycle. The Q3 FY2023 release narrowed the full-year FY2023 revenue outlook to $23.7–$24.0 billion. That fiscal year ended before the target quarter began.

April 20, 2023, immediately preceding earnings release. Management forecast $21.7–$22.1 billion of total FY2024 revenue and gave annual ranges for both segments. The release supplied no Q1 consolidated revenue ceiling.

The April 20 earnings-call presentation also labeled the $21.7–$22.1 billion range as FY2024 guidance. The search of management’s public call remarks and investor presentations identified no earlier explicit Q1 consolidated revenue bound.
The intervening May 2 Form 8-K disclosed the CFO’s retention incentive agreement. It contained no quarterly sales update.
Rite Aid’s June 12 announcement identified June 3 as the FY2024 first-quarter end and scheduled the results for June 29. It gave no preliminary revenue figure.
EDGAR accepted the June 29 results 8-K at 07:06:15 that day and lists the earnings release as Exhibit 99.1.

The July 11 Form 10-Q confirms both reported amounts. Its segment table reconciles Q1 FY2024 retail pharmacy revenue of $4,492,329,000 plus pharmacy services revenue of $1,196,154,000 less $35,321,000 of intersegment eliminations to $5,653,162,000 consolidated.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Rite Aid dated Exhibit 99.1 June 29, 2023 and said it was reporting the first-quarter results that day. The same-day EDGAR acceptance independently confirms public availability.

independent_review.basis: April 30, 2025 is the earliest qualifying disclosure I verified. Tennant’s consolidated income statement reports Q1 2025 net sales of $290.0 million against $311.0 million in Q1 2024, below the $295.45 million cutoff by $5.45 million. The onset date remains unverified because management announced a March 20 C.L. King investor conference, and I could not verify whether Tennant made public quarter-specific sales remarks there.

coverage.detail: October 31, 2024. The Q3 release reaffirmed fiscal 2024 guidance. It supplied no Q1 2025 consolidated sales bound.
The January 2025 Needham presentation showed a $1.293 billion estimated fiscal 2024 sales figure. It supplied no numeric Q1 2025 sales ceiling.
February 17, 2025. The preceding earnings release gave a fiscal 2025 net sales range of $1.210 billion to $1.250 billion. Neither endpoint applied to Q1.

February 18 earnings call, checked through a third-party transcript of management’s remarks. The CFO described Q1 and Q3 as seasonally lower-volume quarters without quantifying Q1 sales. The CEO announced virtual investor conferences for March 19 and March 20. I could not locate public remarks, a replay, or an event-specific presentation for the March 20 C.L. King event.
Tennant’s March 2025 investor deck showed estimated net sales by year and long-term growth objectives. It supplied no Q1 2025 consolidated sales ceiling.

March 19 Sidoti conference, checked through a third-party transcript. The CEO discussed a full-year sales decline and expected 5% to 6% order growth for 2025. Neither figure bounded Q1 reported revenue.
April 17. Tennant scheduled the Q1 release for April 30 after market close and the call for May 1. The notice contained no preliminary sales figure.

April 30 results release, Exhibit 99.1. The consolidated income statement gives $290.0 million and $311.0 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. The reported decline of 6.8% includes the 5.0% organic decline, a 0.3% acquisition contribution and a 2.1% currency headwind.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Tennant’s IR results page displays 04/30/2025, and the SEC exhibit carries an April 30, 2025 dateline. These establish publication of the actual sales figure that day. The unresolved March 20 conference coverage prevents verification that April 30 was first.

independent_review.basis: February 23, 2026 is the earliest qualifying disclosure I could verify. Tennant’s GAAP earnings table reports consolidated net sales of $291.6 million for the three months ended December 31, 2025, versus $328.9 million a year earlier. The reported decline was 11.3%, and sales were below the $312.455 million cutoff. The date remains null because management announced three intervening investor conferences and I could not verify the content of any public Tennant remarks or materials from those events.

coverage.detail: August 6, 2025 Q2 release. Tennant reaffirmed full-year net sales guidance of $1.21–$1.25 billion. Neither the release nor the August 7 earnings-call remarks reviewed supplied a qualifying Q4 sales ceiling.

November 3 Q3 release. Tennant reaffirmed the annual range and reported nine-month net sales of $911.9 million. Subtraction implies Q4 sales of $298.1–$338.1 million. The implied high end exceeds $312.455 million, and the published guidance was annual.
The Q3 call slides anticipated Q4 momentum and favorable exchange rates that would keep full-year sales within guidance. Slide 5 gave no numeric ceiling for Q4 reported net sales.

On the November 4 public call, CEO Dave Huml said approximately $318 million of Q4 sales would deliver the guidance midpoint. That exceeds the cutoff. His roughly $311 million figure was a prior-year comparison adjusted for backlog reduction. He announced Baird on November 13, ROTH on November 19 and Oppenheimer on December 11. Searches did not locate issuer slides, recordings or transcripts establishing what Tennant publicly disclosed at those events.
The February 12 interim 8-K’s Regulation FD disclosure concerned board appointments and a cooperation agreement. It supplied no Q4 net sales figure.
The February 17 notice scheduled results for after market close February 23 and the call for February 24. It gave no preliminary Q4 sales figure.

The February 23 issuer release directly compares both quarters on a consolidated reported basis. Its sales bridge shows an 11.3% reported decline, a 13.9% organic decline, a 2.6% currency benefit and zero quarterly acquisition contribution.
EDGAR accepted the results 8-K at 19:02:30 on February 23 and assigned a February 24 filing date. The index identifies Exhibit 99.1 as the February 23 news release.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Tennant’s IR release displays 02/23/2026, and Item 2.02 of its 8-K states that the company issued the release on February 23. That verifies publication of the actuals. The unresolved question is whether an earlier public conference disclosure qualified.

independent_review.basis: The May 9 Form 10-Q was the earliest verified public issuer communication to establish the threshold on a consolidated total-revenue basis. It reported $153,175,000 for Q1 2024 versus $162,092,000 for Q1 2023, a 5.50% decline. The actual was $812,400 below the $153,987,400 cutoff. The April 24 earnings release disclosed product sales alone and gave no upper bound for rental and royalty revenue.

coverage.detail: October 25, 2023, Q3 release. Management expected earlier Halloween shipments to weigh on Q4 2023 sales. It gave no numeric Q1 2024 revenue outlook.
February 16, 2024, Q4 and full-year release. Management reported Q4 2023 net product sales of $195,368,000 and discussed 2024 supply conditions without giving a Q1 2024 revenue figure or range.

The 2023 annual report to shareholders, submitted March 25, includes the year-end Form 10-K. Its Q1 2024 discussion addressed Canadian labor negotiations. The report supplied no numeric upper bound for quarterly revenue.

April 24, 2024, Q1 earnings release. The table labels $151,464,000 and $160,711,000 as Net Product Sales. To establish the total-revenue cutoff on April 24, the release would also have needed to establish rental and royalty revenue of at most $2,523,400. It supplied no such figure or ceiling.

The issuer's account of its May 6 annual meeting records director elections and auditor ratification. Searches for interim guidance, preliminary results, investor presentations and dated public management remarks or calls found no earlier disclosure giving a qualifying Q1 total-revenue figure.

The Q1 10-Q earnings table reconciles both periods. Q1 2024 product sales of $151,464,000 plus rental and royalty revenue of $1,711,000 totaled $153,175,000. Q1 2023 product sales of $160,711,000 plus $1,381,000 totaled $162,092,000.
EDGAR records the Q1 Form 10-Q as accepted May 9, 2024 at 15:00:40 for the period ended March 31, 2024.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: EDGAR shows both acceptance and filing on May 9, 2024. The earlier earnings exhibit is dated April 24 for immediate release, but its 6% decline applies only to net product sales.

independent_review.basis: Union Pacific’s October 19 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its consolidated income statement reports Q3 2023 total operating revenue of $5,941 million against $6,566 million in Q3 2022. Both figures include freight and other revenue. The reported actual was $296.7 million below the $6,237.7 million threshold, a 9.52% year-over-year decline.

coverage.detail: April 20, preceding earnings cycle. Full-year guidance covered carloads, operating ratio, pricing and capital allocation. The 15% figure was a capital-spending ceiling expressed as a share of revenue. The release gave no Q3 revenue bound.

June 13, Wells Fargo conference disclosure. The CFO quantified a Q2 labor expense of about $70 million and a Q2 tax benefit of nearly $75 million, and updated the full-year operating-ratio outlook. None established Q3 revenue.

independent_review.basis: Insight’s August 1 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. independent_review.basis: First Solar’s Q3 results release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its consolidated statement of operations reports net sales of $583,504,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2021 and $927,565,000 for the same quarter in 2020. The reported actual was 37.09% lower year over year and below the $881,186,750 cutoff. Both figures use the comparative GAAP net sales line as presented after the 2021 business disposals.

coverage.detail: April 29, Q1 earnings release. First Solar guided to $2.85 billion–$3.025 billion in full-year 2021 net sales. It also reported closing the U.S. project development and North American O&M business sales. The release gave no Q3 consolidated sales ceiling.

April 29, Q1 earnings presentation. The sales guidance table covers full-year 2021. Management’s call discussion of second-half segment timing supplied no numeric upper bound for Q3 consolidated revenue.

July 29, Q2 earnings release. First Solar raised full-year net sales guidance to $2.875 billion–$3.1 billion. Subtracting first-half actuals from that range yields a combined Q3–Q4 outlook and leaves the Q3 amount unspecified.

July 29, Q2 earnings presentation. The numeric sales outlook was for 2021. On the accompanying call, the CFO expected most remaining systems-segment revenue and gross margin in Q4. That timing remark supplied no numeric ceiling for Q3 consolidated net sales.

The historical filing chronology shows the July 29 earnings 8-K, the July 30 10-Q, and then the November 4 earnings 8-K, with no intervening 8-K. Searches for interim releases, investor presentations and public management remarks found no earlier explicit Q3 consolidated sales bound.
October 21, issuer scheduling notice. First Solar identified the September 30 quarter and announced a November 4 release after market close. The notice gave no preliminary sales figure or range.

November 4, Q3 earnings release, Exhibit 99.1. The consolidated net sales row gives 583,504 and 927,565 in thousands of dollars for Q3 2021 and Q3 2020, respectively. The headline rounds Q3 2021 sales to $584 million.
The original wire release identifies First Solar as its source and records publication on November 4, 2021 at 4:05 p.m. ET.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: First Solar’s Exhibit 99.1 bears a November 4, 2021 dateline. The issuer’s wire timestamp establishes public availability at 4:05 p.m. ET that day, before the 4:30 p.m. earnings call and the November 5 Form 10-Q filing.

independent_review.basis: First Solar’s Q1 2022 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. The reported Q1 2022 amount was 45.69% of prior-year sales, below the $763,205,300 cutoff. Both figures come from the same consolidated net-sales row. Gains on business sales appear separately.

coverage.detail: November 4, 2021, preceding earnings cycle. First Solar retained its $2.875 billion to $3.1 billion net-sales range for fiscal 2021. That range ended with the December 2021 quarter and provided no bound for Q1 2022.
March 1, 2022, immediately preceding earnings release. First Solar forecast $2.4 billion to $2.6 billion of fiscal 2022 net sales. It gave no quarterly allocation or numeric Q1 net-sales ceiling.

The March 1 issuer presentation gave annual shipment guidance of 8.9 to 9.4 GW. It treated the potential Japan business sale as an estimated gain of $270 million to $290 million. Neither figure bounded Q1 consolidated net sales.
On the March 1 public call, management repeated the annual sales range and discussed earnings improving over the course of 2022. The remarks supplied no numeric upper bound for Q1 net sales.
The intervening Form 8-K, dated April 1, concerned a director’s March 29 notice that she would not stand for reelection. It contained no preliminary results or sales update.
The April 12 joint announcement covered a 4 GW order for deliveries in 2023 through 2025. It supplied no Q1 2022 revenue figure.
The April 14 investor notice scheduled the Q1 results for April 28 after market close. It gave no sales amount.
April 28 actuals. Exhibit 99.1 gives the explicit Q1 figure as 367,040 in thousands of dollars and the year-ago figure as 803,374 in the same units. The $907,319,000 middle column is Q4 2021.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Exhibit 99.1 is datelined April 28, 2022 and says First Solar announced results that day. Item 2.02 of the accompanying Form 8-K independently identifies April 28 as the press-release date for the quarter ended March 31. The 10-Q followed on April 29.

independent_review.basis: On April 17, Douglas Dynamics reported preliminary consolidated net sales of $82.5 million for the quarter ended March 31, 2023. That explicit point estimate was below $97,470,950, the threshold equal to 95% of Q1 2022 reported net sales of $102,601,000. The April release gave sales to the nearest $0.1 million. The May 1 GAAP table later confirmed $82,545,000.

coverage.detail: October 31, 2022, Q3 release. The $600 million to $630 million net-sales outlook covered fiscal 2022. Management expected headwinds to persist into 2023 but supplied no Q1 2023 sales bound.
February 20, 2023, Q4 and full-year release. Management projected $620 million to $680 million of fiscal 2023 net sales. The release gave no Q1 consolidated net-sales range.

February 21 earnings call, management remarks in the published transcript. Asked directly how to model Q1, CFO Sarah Lauber said snowfall was affecting the business and gave no numeric Q1 sales estimate. She later confirmed the guidance covered the full fiscal year.
The issuer's event calendar lists the November 1 and February 21 earnings calls. Its next listed event after February 21 was the April 25 shareholder meeting, after the preliminary release.
Sidoti's published March 22–23 conference agenda lists Douglas Dynamics under one-on-one meetings only. The agenda identifies no public company presentation.

The issuer's intervening March 27 announcement concerned its 2022 ESG report. The release archive and searches for interim presentations and public management remarks yielded no earlier numeric Q1 consolidated sales bound.

April 17 preliminary release. The quarterly consolidated table gives Q1 2023 net sales of $82.5 million against $102.6 million a year earlier. The separate $620 million to $650 million range covers full-year 2023.
May 1 actual-results release. The consolidated statements of loss report net sales, in thousands, of 82,545 and 102,601 for the three months ended March 31, 2023 and 2022, respectively.

The May 2 Form 10-Q confirms both totals on the same two-segment reporting perimeter. In thousands, Work Truck Attachments and Work Truck Solutions contributed 19,246 and 63,299 in Q1 2023, versus 45,776 and 56,825 in Q1 2022.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Douglas Dynamics' investor-relations page explicitly states “Released April 17, 2023.” The SEC exhibit carries the same April 17 dateline and identifies March 31 as the quarter end.

independent_review.basis: The October 30 actuals qualify. The consolidated income statement reports Q3 2023 net sales of $144,121,000 against $166,100,000 for Q3 2022, a 13.23% decline. The 95% cutoff was $157,795,000. The earliest qualifying date remains unverified because the September investor presentation and accompanying management remarks could not be fully checked.

coverage.detail: April 17 preliminary results covered the quarter ended March 31. The revised sales outlook covered full-year 2023.
May 1 Q1 results gave a full-year sales range of $620 million to $650 million. Management expected lower preseason orders in Work Truck Attachments but gave no consolidated Q3 sales ceiling.

July 31 Q2 results retained the $620 million to $650 million annual range. The approximately 60/40 split described Q2 and Q3 preseason revenue in Attachments. The other Q3 comparison concerned segment EBITDA margin. Neither figure bounded consolidated Q3 sales.

On the August 1 earnings call, management again described the 60/40 split as preseason shipments and discussed uncertainty about late-Q3 reorders. The transcript gives no explicit consolidated Q3 sales ceiling.
The September 20 Form 8-K identifies a presentation dated September 18 for the September 20–22 D.A. Davidson conference. The filing itself gives no Q3 sales figure.

Exhibit 99.1 contains 20 image-based slides. I could verify the exhibit’s identity but could not read the full deck or locate a public transcript of the conference remarks. Whether that communication supplied an earlier numeric bound remains unresolved.
The issuer’s archive lists two releases between the July 31 and October 30 results. September 6 announced a dividend. October 17 scheduled the Q3 release and call.

The October 30 release gives net sales of 144,121 and 166,100, in thousands of dollars, in the three-month columns for September 30, 2023 and 2022. Both figures come from the same consolidated GAAP statement.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: The issuer’s release archive timestamps the actual results at October 30, 2023, 6:00 p.m. EDT. Both the issuer release and SEC Exhibit 99.1 carry the October 30 dateline. This establishes when the actual became public, while the September disclosure gap prevents assigning the earliest date.

Sales fell 10.22% year over year and were $7,516,950 below the $136,914,950 threshold. The reported actual supplies the explicit numeric upper bound.

coverage.detail: In the April 29 Q1 release and April 30 call, management lowered the high end of its full-year sales outlook from $660 million to $640 million. It discussed weaker preseason orders and the second-half outlook for Work Truck Solutions without giving a numeric ceiling for consolidated Q3 sales.

The issuer’s public event calendar lists the July 30 Q2 call followed by the October 29 Q3 call. The intervening disclosure search found no investor presentation, public management update, or preliminary results giving a numeric upper bound for consolidated Q3 sales.
The Q3 dividend announcement disclosed a per-share cash dividend and gave no sales outlook.

The September 11 announcement concerned a $64.2 million sale and leaseback of seven facilities. The Q3 income statement recorded the $42.298 million gain separately below gross profit, leaving the consolidated net-sales comparison intact.
The September 17 release announced executive appointments and a retirement. It gave no Q3 revenue estimate.
The October 15 notice scheduled Q3 results for after market close on October 28 and the call for October 29. It disclosed no preliminary sales figure.
Page 8 of the October 28 earnings release, furnished as Exhibit 99.1, gives the precise quarterly net-sales figures of 129,398 and 144,121 in thousands of dollars.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: The issuer’s earnings release is datelined October 28, 2024, and its press-release archive records publication at 6:05 p.m. EDT that day. The October 29 earnings call and Form 10-Q followed the public release.

independent_review.basis: GameStop’s fiscal Q3 2022 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. coverage.detail: June 1, preceding earnings cycle. The Q1 release reported $1.378 billion in Q1 net sales. Its forward-looking discussion identified a planned Q2 marketplace launch and gave no Q3 sales estimate.
June 1 Q1 call, as transcribed. Management explicitly said it was not providing formal guidance and gave no numeric Q3 sales bound.
September 7, immediately preceding earnings release. GameStop reported $1,136.0 million in net sales for Q2, which ended July 30. It supplied no fiscal Q3 consolidated sales outlook.
September 7 Q2 call, as transcribed. Management explicitly said it was not providing formal guidance and gave no numeric Q3 sales bound.
September 7 partnership announcement. GameStop described plans to carry FTX gift cards, withheld the financial terms and gave no quarterly sales forecast.
October 31, two days after quarter end. The marketplace announcement discussed games, digital assets and customer reach. It gave no preliminary Q3 consolidated sales figure.
November 28. GameStop scheduled the Q3 results for after market close on December 7 and provided call details. It disclosed no sales figure or range.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: GameStop’s Exhibit 99.1 carries a December 7, 2022 dateline and says the company released fiscal Q3 results that day. The same-day EDGAR acceptance independently confirms public availability.

independent_review.basis: GameStop’s June 7 results release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. The reported amount was 89.75% of prior-year sales, below the $1,309.48 million threshold.

coverage.detail: December 7, 2022, preceding earnings cycle. The Q3 FY2022 release reported the quarter ended October 29, 2022 and gave no numeric Q1 FY2023 sales outlook. On the [earnings call](https://6ix.com/event/gamestop-corporation-gme-q3-2022-earnings-call), CEO Matt Furlong said the company was not providing formal guidance.

March 21, 2023, immediately preceding earnings release. GameStop reported Q4 FY2022 net sales of $2,226.4 million and full-year sales of $5,927.2 million. It gave no Q1 FY2023 sales range. On the [earnings call](https://6ix.com/event/gamestop-corporation-gme-q4-2022-earnings-call), Furlong anticipated Q1 transformation charges and explicitly declined to give guidance.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: The issuer’s release is dated June 7, 2023 and says GameStop released results that day for the first quarter ended April 29, 2023. Item 2.02 of the contemporaneous Form 8-K independently confirms the June 7 issuance date.

independent_review.basis: GameStop’s fiscal Q3 2023 results release was the earliest qualifying issuer communication found. Its consolidated GAAP net sales table reports $1,078.3 million for the 13 weeks ended October 28, 2023, versus $1,186.4 million for the 13 weeks ended October 29, 2022. The reported amount was below the $1,127.08 million threshold, a 9.11% year-over-year decline. The search of earlier releases, SEC disclosures, investor presentations and public management remarks found no explicit numeric upper bound for Q3 consolidated sales.

coverage.detail: June 7, preceding earnings cycle. GameStop reported Q1 sales and anticipated further European restructuring charges in Q2. It gave no Q3 sales figure and said it would hold no earnings call that day.

September 6, immediately preceding earnings release. GameStop reported Q2 net sales of $1,163.8 million against $1,136.0 million. It gave no Q3 sales outlook and said it would hold no earnings call that day.
The Q2 Form 10-Q confirmed that all Irish stores closed in Q2. Its discussion of store closures and cost reductions supplied no numeric bound for consolidated Q3 sales.
September 28, interim Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1. GameStop announced Ryan Cohen’s appointment as CEO and provided no quarterly sales update.
November 22, after quarter end. GameStop scheduled the Q3 results for December 6 after market close. The notice contained no preliminary sales figure.
December 6, actual results. The 13-week net sales row gives $1,078.3 million and the corresponding prior-year $1,186.4 million on the same consolidated GAAP statement.
EDGAR records acceptance of the results Form 8-K at 16:10:54 on December 6, 2023, and identifies the Q3 earnings release as Exhibit 99.1.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: GameStop’s investor-relations release carries a December 6, 2023 dateline and states that the company released the results that day. The same-day EDGAR acceptance independently confirms public availability.

independent_review.basis: GameStop’s March 24 earnings release was the earliest qualifying issuer communication found. Its consolidated GAAP net-sales row reports $1,104.3 million for the 13 weeks ended January 31, 2026 (fiscal Q4 2025), versus $1,282.6 million for the 13 weeks ended February 1, 2025. The actual was 13.90% lower and below the $1,218.47 million threshold. Both figures use GameStop’s reported consolidated perimeter, including Canadian sales of zero and $77.7 million, respectively.

coverage.detail: September 9, 2025. The preceding earnings cycle reported Q2 net sales of $972.2 million and gave no numerical Q4 sales outlook.
October 7, 2025. The intervening 8-K announced a warrant distribution and gave no Q4 sales estimate.
December 9, 2025. The immediately preceding earnings release reported Q3 net sales of $821.0 million versus $860.3 million. It gave no Q4 revenue range or year-over-year sales bound.

The Q3 10-Q reported nine-month net sales of $2,525.6 million and discussed holiday seasonality. A retrospective cross-check using the March 24 annual actual gives $3,629.9 million less $2,525.6 million, or $1,104.3 million. The December filing supplied no explicit Q4 sales bound.

January 7, 2026. The CEO award release set market-capitalization and cumulative performance EBITDA targets. Its operating comparisons used trailing periods and supplied no fiscal Q4 net-sales estimate.
January 8, 2026. The follow-up 8-K furnished the CEO option agreement. This and the January 7 filing were the two intervening 8-Ks between the Q3 and Q4 results.

March 16, 2026. GameStop announced that it would report after market close on March 24 and supplied no preliminary figures. Searches for interim guidance, investor presentations, calls and dated management remarks found no earlier explicit Q4 consolidated sales bound.

March 24, 2026. The issuer’s quarterly statements give the explicit $1,104.3 million actual. The geographic table independently sums to the same consolidated total and retains the $1,282.6 million prior-year comparator.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: GameStop’s investor-relations release displays March 24, 2026. The same release in SEC Exhibit 99.1 carries a March 24, 2026 Business Wire dateline and states that GameStop released the results that day.

independent_review.basis: Celsius first established the threshold in its Q3 2024 earnings release. The consolidated GAAP revenue row, in thousands of dollars, reports 265,748 for the three months ended September 30, 2024 and 384,757 for the same three months in 2023. Actual revenue of $265,748,000 was below the $365,519,150 cutoff. The September warnings quantified the decline in Pepsi orders and left revenue from other customers unbounded.

coverage.detail: May 7, preceding earnings cycle. Celsius reported Q1 revenue of $355.7 million, up 37% year over year. The release gave no numeric Q3 consolidated revenue outlook.
August 6, Q2 earnings release. Celsius reported $402.0 million for Q2 and $757.7 million for the first half. It gave no upper bound for Q3 consolidated revenue.
The August investor presentation charted consolidated revenue through Q2 2024. Its $384.8 million Q3 figure was the historical Q3 2023 comparison.

On the August 6 call, an analyst asked whether a $20 million inventory headwind would carry into Q3. The CFO explained that the $20 million to $30 million estimate discussed in June concerned Q2 and that Q3 would depend on the distributor’s ordering decisions.
August 28. Celsius announced public September 4 and September 10 webcasts to discuss Q3 business and inventory trends. The announcement contained no revenue estimate.

September 4, Barclays. Management specified that the $100 million to $120 million year-over-year reduction represented Q3 orders to Pepsi. The roughly 10% growth figure described quarter-to-date retail performance. Neither figure set a ceiling on full-quarter consolidated GAAP revenue.

September 10, Piper Sandler. In the transcript of the public remarks, management again attributed the $100 million to $120 million decrease to Pepsi purchases and distinguished those orders from sales at the register. It supplied no consolidated Q3 revenue bound. The issuer’s August 28 notice confirms the public webcast date.
September 19. The intervening Form 8-K reported an Item 5.02 personnel matter and contained no earnings exhibit.
October 30. Celsius scheduled its Q3 release for before market open on November 6. The notice contained no preliminary sales figure.
November 6. The issuer published both quarterly amounts in the same consolidated revenue row and summarized the year-over-year decline as 31%.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: The earnings release carries a November 6, 2024 dateline. Item 2.02 of Celsius’s Form 8-K independently states that Celsius issued the Q3 release on November 6. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1341766/000134176624000095/celh-20241106.htm

independent_review.basis: Celsius publicly established the threshold crossing by May 6, 2025. Its consolidated GAAP revenue for the three months ended March 31, 2025 was $329,276,000, down 7.43% from $355,708,000 a year earlier and $8,646,600 below the $337,922,600 cutoff. The earliest disclosure date remains unverified because I could not verify management’s full remarks at the March 18 Roth fireside chat.

coverage.detail: November 6, 2024, preceding earnings cycle. The $123.9 million decline concerned sales to the largest distributor in Q3 2024. The release gave no numeric Q1 2025 consolidated revenue ceiling.
On the November 6 call, management discussed retail scan trends, promotions and distribution plans heading into 2025 without quantifying consolidated Q1 2025 revenue.
February 20, 2025, immediately preceding earnings release. The $332.2 million figure was Q4 2024 actual revenue. The release gave no numeric Q1 2025 consolidated revenue outlook.

On the February 20 call, the CEO acknowledged a slow start to 2025. The CFO’s $8 million to $10 million response concerned the Q4 distributor inventory impact. Neither statement set a Q1 consolidated revenue ceiling.

February 21 CAGNY presentation, furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The slides identified $1.36 billion as FY2024 revenue and presented acquisition metrics based on Alani’s 2024 financials. I found no explicit Q1 2025 consolidated revenue bound in the slides.
March 12 UBS fireside chat. The issuer confirms the public event and time. The available transcript discusses retail sales velocity and market share. I found no qualifying quarterly revenue figure.

The March 10 issuer notice scheduled the Roth fireside chat for March 18 at approximately 3:30 p.m. ET and identified public webcasts as a channel for material disclosures. The notice contains no sales forecast. I could not verify the complete Roth replay or transcript to determine whether management gave a numeric ceiling during the chat.

April 1 acquisition closing. Alani closed one day after the March 31 quarter end, so its sales are excluded from Celsius’s reported Q1 revenue. Combined-brand figures cannot establish the threshold crossing.
The May 1 notice announced the May 6 earnings release date without providing preliminary quarterly revenue.

May 6 earnings release, Exhibit 99.1. The consolidated statements of operations report revenue in thousands of $329,276 for Q1 2025 and $355,708 for Q1 2024. The exact reported actual is the numeric bound recorded here.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: The issuer’s Q1 earnings release is dated May 6, 2025, states that Celsius reported results that day, and lists the same day’s 8:00 a.m. ET webcast. This verifies the publication date of the actuals. The unresolved March 18 remarks prevent assigning May 6 as the earliest qualifying date.

independent_review.basis: FET’s October 30 earnings release first established that Q3 2025 consolidated GAAP revenue met the cutoff. Its income statement reported $196,231,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025 and $207,806,000 for the same quarter in 2024. Revenue fell 5.57%, coming in $1,184,700 below the $197,415,700 cutoff. The earlier Q3 revenue forecast extended to $200,000,000.

coverage.detail: May 1 Q1 release. FET guided to Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $18–22 million and full-year free cash flow of $40–60 million. It gave no Q3 revenue ceiling.
May 2 Q1 call. Management said revenue could begin declining in Q3 if oil prices failed to rebound. It supplied no numeric upper bound for the quarter.
June 11 Sidoti investor presentation. The 2025 forecast ranges covered adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow. The slides supplied no Q3 consolidated revenue ceiling.
June 11 public remarks. Management repeated the conditional Q3 revenue-decline scenario from May without quantifying the decline.
August 7 Q2 release. The explicit Q3 range of $19–23 million applied to adjusted EBITDA. The release gave no Q3 revenue range.

August 8 Q2 call. CFO Lyle Williams forecast Q3 revenue of $180–200 million. The $200 million upper end exceeded the cutoff by $2,584,300. He separately forecast full-year revenue of $760–800 million.
August 18 announcement covered FET’s secondary stock listing and supplied no revenue update.
September 16 issuer notice identified the September 18 public Water Tower Research fireside chat with the CEO and CFO.

September 18 chat. The CFO’s roughly 5% decline referred to industry activity versus Q1 levels. Management discussed full-year EBITDA and cash flow and supplied no revised numeric Q3 consolidated revenue ceiling.
October 6 notice scheduled the October 31 earnings call and said results would be released beforehand. It gave no preliminary revenue figure.
The October 30 release, furnished as Exhibit 99.1, shows 196,231 and 207,806 in the consolidated revenue row, in thousands of dollars, for Q3 2025 and Q3 2024 respectively.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: FET’s IR release displays October 30, 2025 in both the page date and the Houston announcement dateline. EDGAR records October 30 as the 8-K’s report date and October 31 as its filing date. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1401257/000140125725000106/0001401257-25-000106-index.htm

independent_review.basis: MACOM’s fiscal Q3 results release was the earliest verified communication with an explicit figure covering the full reported quarter. Consolidated GAAP revenue was $148,522,000 for the three months ended June 30, 2023, down 13.8% from $172,259,000 for the three months ended July 1, 2022. The 95% cutoff was $163,646,050. The May 4 guidance capped revenue at $150,000,000 but expressly excluded OMMIC, whose acquisition closed during Q3. MACOM gave no numeric ceiling for the excluded contribution.

coverage.detail: February 2, preceding earnings cycle. MACOM guided revenue to $166 million–$170 million for fiscal Q2 ending March 31. The release gave no June-quarter range.

May 4, Q2 earnings release. The June-quarter outlook was $145 million–$150 million and explicitly excluded all revenue contributions from the pending OMMIC acquisition. At the high end, an OMMIC contribution of up to $13,646,050 would have kept consolidated revenue within the cutoff. That amount is calculated headroom, not an issuer forecast.

May 4 public earnings call, as transcribed. Management expected the acquisition to close in fiscal Q3, described its near-term revenue impact as small in qualitative terms, and repeated the exclusion when giving guidance. The call supplied no numeric upper bound for OMMIC.

May 31, MACOM announced completion of the OMMIC acquisition. The announcement described the acquired facilities and products and gave neither an OMMIC revenue estimate nor a revised consolidated Q3 range.

July 20, MACOM announced the August 3 results date without giving preliminary sales. Searches for intervening guidance, 8-K exhibits, investor presentations and public management remarks found no earlier explicit Q3 revenue ceiling that included OMMIC.
August 3, actual results. The condensed consolidated statements of operations give June 2023 revenue of 148,522 and July 2022 revenue of 172,259, both in thousands of dollars.

The Q3 10-Q confirms the May 31 closing. Note 3 describes the acquired operation’s post-acquisition results as immaterial to the consolidated financial statements. That retrospective assessment supplies no numeric bound for the May 4 outlook.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: MACOM’s investor-relations results page displays “Aug 03, 2023” and carries an August 3 newswire dateline. The same earnings release was furnished as SEC Exhibit 99.1.

independent_review.basis: Block’s May 5 shareholder letter was the earliest qualifying communication found. On the November 4 call, management projected approximately 40% growth in full-year 2022 non-GAAP operating expenses and identified Q1 2022 as the expected Afterpay closing period. Neither figure bounded quarterly revenue.

February 24, 2022 Q4 release, pages 20–21. Block expected 35% year-over-year growth in Square payment volume for January and February combined, growth in Cash App gross profit, and an approximately $180 million sequential increase in Q1 non-GAAP operating expenses including Afterpay. None established a Q1 consolidated revenue ceiling.

On the February 24 call, the CFO discussed January gross profit and February estimates, including improving Cash App inflows. Management gave no numeric upper bound for full-quarter consolidated revenue.
The April 4 Form 8-K disclosed a Cash App Investing customer-data incident. It gave no quarterly sales estimate.
Block’s pre-results scheduling notice, distributed by Business Wire, announced a May 5 after-market release and webcast. It contained no preliminary results.
