The public transcript index places the February 24 and May 5 earnings calls consecutively. The next investor presentation listed was the May 18 Investor Day. The intervening search found no preliminary release, presentation or dated management remarks with a qualifying bound.

May 5 actuals. The consolidated statement of operations gives the exact total for each quarter in thousands of dollars. The reconciliation also explicitly labels those same figures GAAP and identifies the bitcoin and Afterpay contributions.
Item 2.02 confirms that Block issued the Q1 shareholder letter on May 5, 2022 and furnished it as Exhibit 99.1.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Block’s contemporaneous Form 8-K explicitly dates issuance of the shareholder letter to May 5, 2022 and identifies the reported quarter as the one ended March 31, 2022.

independent_review.basis: Guidewire’s June 2 earnings release explicitly forecast “Total revenue between $218 million and $224 million” for fiscal Q4 2021, the three months ending July 31. The $224,000,000 upper bound was $7,490,300 below the cutoff of $231,490,300, or 95% of the prior-year quarter’s $243,674,000 consolidated GAAP revenue.

coverage.detail: March 4, preceding earnings cycle. Guidewire forecast Q3 revenue of $155–159 million and FY2021 revenue of $725–733 million. With first-half actuals of $349.864 million, those forecasts mathematically implied a Q4 maximum of $228.136 million ($733 million minus $349.864 million minus $155 million). The release gave no explicit Q4 total-revenue bound.

On the March 4 earnings call, the CFO discussed removing roughly $4 million of previously expected Q4 billable travel and expenses from the services forecast. His remarks gave no numeric upper bound for Q4 consolidated revenue.

June 2, first qualifying disclosure. The Business Outlook section gave the explicit $218–224 million Q4 total-revenue range and listed ARR separately. As a cross-check, the $738 million FY2021 high end less $513.832 million of nine-month revenue implied $224.168 million. The selected $224 million comes directly from the quarterly outlook.
Guidewire’s June 1 notice scheduled the CEO’s William Blair presentation for June 3. The notice contained no Q4 revenue forecast, and the presentation followed the June 2 release.
Guidewire also announced a June 30 BofA InsurTech presentation. The event followed the qualifying disclosure.
August 19. Guidewire scheduled the September 2 results release and call. The notice contained no preliminary revenue figure.
Guidewire’s acquisition disclosure dates the HazardHub closing to August 18, 2021, after the July 31 quarter end. HazardHub therefore contributed no revenue to the target quarter.

September 2 actuals. The consolidated statements of operations report total revenue of $229,435,000 for the three months ended July 31, 2021 and $243,674,000 for the comparable 2020 quarter. Actual revenue exceeded June’s guidance but remained below the $231,490,300 cutoff.
EDGAR identifies the June 2 release as Exhibit 99.1 to Guidewire’s Item 2.02 Form 8-K and records acceptance on June 2 at 16:16:10.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Guidewire datelined the qualifying release June 2, 2021. EDGAR independently records the release as a public Form 8-K exhibit accepted that same day.

independent_review.basis: SEACOR Marine’s Q3 earnings release was the earliest qualifying issuer communication found. Its consolidated income statement reports operating revenues of $68,916,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2024 and $76,900,000 for the same quarter of 2023. The reported actual was below the $73,055,000 threshold (95% of $76,900,000), a 10.4% year-over-year decline.

coverage.detail: May 1, preceding earnings cycle. The CEO expected utilization to improve as vessels completed repositioning and entered new contracts. The release gave no numeric Q3 consolidated revenue outlook.
The July 3 Form 8-K confirms that the company posted its July 2 investor presentation publicly on July 3.
The July presentation showed Q1 operating revenue of $62.770 million and contract backlog exceeding $440 million including options. Neither figure supplied a Q3 revenue ceiling.

July 31, immediately preceding earnings release. The CEO reported $403.9 million of backlog including options, with contracts averaging approximately one year, and expected utilization to improve over the rest of 2024. He gave no numeric Q3 consolidated revenue range.

The CEO’s September 11 Pareto Securities Energy Conference presentation showed contract backlog exceeding $400 million including options. It gave no numeric upper bound for Q3 consolidated revenue. The search found no separate dated public management remarks or preliminary results establishing one before October 30.
The September 19 Form 8-K and its exhibit announcement concerned the appointment of Lisa P. Young to the board. The filing gave no quarterly sales update.

October 30 actuals. The Operating Revenues row in the unaudited condensed consolidated income statement shows 68,916 and 76,900 in thousands of dollars under the respective 2024 and 2023 three-month columns. Gains and losses on asset dispositions appear separately.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: The issuer’s Q3 results page is timestamped October 30, 2024 at 4:27 PM EDT. Its dateline confirms that SEACOR Marine announced the results that day for the quarter ended September 30, 2024.

independent_review.basis: SEACOR Marine’s first-quarter results release was the earliest qualifying communication found. Its consolidated GAAP income statement reports operating revenues of $55,499,000 for the three months ended March 31, 2025, versus $62,770,000 for the same quarter of 2024. The reported amount was $4,132,500 below the $59,631,500 threshold, an 11.6% year-over-year decline. Both figures come from the same comparative revenue line. The statement records gains on asset dispositions separately.

coverage.detail: October 30, 2024. The Q3 release reported a 10.4% revenue decline for Q3 2024. The CEO discussed more than $360 million of contracted backlog including options and inquiries for 2025–2026 work. Neither supplied a Q1 2025 consolidated revenue ceiling.

December 2024 investor presentation. Management discussed refinancing, vessel sales, contract backlog and the expected end of anchor-handling vessel operations by January 2025. It gave no consolidated Q1 revenue estimate.

February 26, 2025. The preceding earnings release reported $69.8 million of Q4 2024 revenue. The CEO described soft North Sea demand and customer delays in Mexico and the U.S. His outlook gave no numeric upper bound for Q1 2025 revenue.
The Form 8-K confirms that SEACOR Marine publicly posted its February investor presentation on February 28, 2025.

The February 28 presentation showed $368 million of multiyear contract backlog including options, with a breakdown by year, and historical FY2024 revenue of $271.4 million. It gave no Q1 2025 consolidated revenue ceiling.
April 4, 2025. The Form 8-K and accompanying release disclosed a $12.9 million repurchase of shares and warrants funded with vessel-sale proceeds. They gave no preliminary quarterly revenue.
April 23, 2025. The annual-meeting proxy covered voting matters and executive compensation. Its first-quarter references supplied no Q1 2025 revenue figure or forecast.

The issuer’s archive lists the December and February presentations, followed by September 2025. It lists no earnings call in the interval. The search for dated public management remarks and preliminary results found no earlier qualifying disclosure.

April 30, 2025. Exhibit 99.1 to the issuer’s Form 8-K reproduces the results release. The consolidated income statement gives operating revenues of 55,499 and 62,770, in thousands of dollars, for Q1 2025 and Q1 2024 respectively.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: The issuer’s investor-relations page timestamps the first-quarter results release April 30, 2025 at 4:27 PM EDT. Exhibit 99.1 also dates the release April 30, 2025.

independent_review.basis: Schneider’s Q1 2023 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its consolidated GAAP income statement reports operating revenues of $1,428.7 million for the three months ended March 31, 2023, and $1,620.5 million for the same quarter of 2022. Both figures include fuel surcharges. The reported actual was 11.84% below the prior year and below the $1,539.475 million threshold.

coverage.detail: October 27, 2022, preceding earnings cycle. Schneider updated full-year 2022 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $2.60–$2.65. Its comments on 2023 described strategic priorities and gave no Q1 2023 consolidated revenue figure.
February 2, 2023, Q4 2022 release. The numeric 2023 outlook covered full-year adjusted diluted EPS of $2.15–$2.35 and net capital expenditures of $525–$575 million. Neither establishes Q1 revenue.

On the February 2 call, management referred investors to slide 26 of its presentation for annual guidance. It said Q1 could be the softest point of 2023 and expected pressure on intermodal volumes. It gave no numeric upper bound for Q1 consolidated operating revenues.
Schneider’s January 25 notice identified two interim public fireside chats with its CEO and CFO, at Evercore on February 8 and Raymond James on March 7.

February 8, Evercore. Management discussed Q4-to-Q1 seasonality qualitatively. The 5% volume decline it cited concerned the prior fourth quarter’s logistics business. The remarks supplied no Q1 consolidated revenue bound.

March 7, Raymond James. Management’s 7.5% figure concerned Q4 intermodal revenue per order. It also discussed bid-season pricing by business line, without giving a numeric Q1 consolidated revenue forecast.
March 30. Schneider scheduled the Q1 results for pre-market release on April 27. The notice contained no preliminary Q1 revenue.
The April 26 Form 8-K reported shareholder voting and a $0.09 second-quarter dividend. It supplied no Q1 sales update.
April 27. EDGAR records acceptance of the earnings Form 8-K at 09:03:00 and identifies Exhibit 99.1 as the results release.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Exhibit 99.1 is datelined April 27, 2023, and says Schneider announced results that day for the three months ended March 31, 2023. The same-day EDGAR acceptance independently confirms public availability.

independent_review.basis: Blue Apron’s August 3 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its consolidated statement of operations reports Q2 2021 net revenue of $124,010,000 versus $131,040,000 for Q2 2020, a 5.36% decline. The actual was $478,000 below the $124,488,000 cutoff. The May 6 forecast straddled that cutoff.

coverage.detail: February 18, preceding earnings cycle. Blue Apron forecast Q1 2021 net revenue of $125 million to $129 million and double-digit revenue growth for full-year 2021. Neither forecast specified Q2 revenue.

May 6, Q1 earnings release. Blue Apron explicitly forecast Q2 net revenue of approximately $122 million to $126 million. The $126 million high end exceeded the cutoff by $1,512,000 and implied only a 3.85% year-over-year decline.

May 6 investor presentation for the Q1 results. Slide 14 covers the Q2 outlook. The search of the presentation and public reporting of management’s earnings call identified no narrower Q2 revenue ceiling.
The June 15 offering announcement and June 16 pricing release, attached as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2, concern a sale of common stock. Neither supplied revised Q2 revenue guidance.
The June offering prospectus supplement also supplied no explicit Q2 revenue ceiling.
July 13, issuer announcement. Blue Apron scheduled the August 3 release and management call without providing preliminary revenue.
The July 30 registration statement concerned shares underlying warrants and supplied no Q2 revenue estimate.

August 3 actuals. The net revenue row for the three months ended June 30 shows 124,010 for 2021 and 131,040 for 2020, in thousands of dollars. Reported revenue includes the approximately $2 million recovery of customer credits described in the release.
The Q2 Form 10-Q confirms both amounts on the same consolidated basis for Blue Apron Holdings and its wholly owned subsidiaries.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: The earnings release is datelined August 3, 2021 and says Blue Apron announced the June-quarter results that day. Item 2.02 of the accompanying Form 8-K confirms issuance of the release, attached as Exhibit 99.1. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1701114/000155837021009858/aprn-20210803x8k.htm

independent_review.basis: Blue Apron’s fourth-quarter earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its consolidated statements of operations report net revenue of $107,007,000 for the three months ended December 31, 2021 and $115,458,000 for the same quarter in 2020. The decline was 7.32%, and the reported amount was below the $109,685,100 threshold.

coverage.detail: August 3, 2021 Q2 release. Blue Apron forecast high-single-digit to low-double-digit FY2021 net revenue growth and expected second-half revenue to grow year over year. Neither forecast supplied a Q4 revenue ceiling.

November 9 Q3 release. The $109,654,000 reported figure was for Q3. The Q4 outlook addressed marketing and discounts. Revenue guidance was single-digit growth for FY2021. With nine-month revenue of $363,370,000, the Q4 cutoff would require FY2021 revenue at or below $473,055,100, about 2.70% above FY2020. The annual outlook allowed growth above that level.

November 9 earnings-call presentation. Slide 6 described increased promotions beginning in Q4 2021 and expected customer and revenue growth starting in 2022. It gave no numeric Q4 consolidated revenue ceiling.

On the November 9 public call, CFO Randy Greben identified Q4 2019 as the relevant comparison for Q4 2021. He gave no numeric Q4 growth endpoint against that base. His single-digit growth outlook applied to FY2021, and his mid-teens discussion applied to FY2022.
The intervening December 16 Form 8-K concerned Delaware stockholder litigation. It contained no preliminary Q4 sales or updated revenue guidance.
Blue Apron’s January 20, 2022 notice scheduled the Q4 release for February 10 before the U.S. market opened. It gave no preliminary revenue figure.
February 10 actual results. The quarterly net-revenue row gives 107,007 and 115,458 in thousands of dollars for Q4 2021 and Q4 2020. The headline’s 13% increase uses Q4 2019 as its base.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Blue Apron’s Exhibit 99.1 is datelined February 10, 2022 and states that it announced the fourth-quarter results that day. Its same-day [Form 8-K, Item 2.02](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1701114/000155837022000980/aprn-20220210x8k.htm) confirms issuance of the release.

independent_review.basis: February 7, 2022 is the earliest qualifying disclosure I verified. Cerence explicitly forecast consolidated GAAP revenue of $82 million to $86 million for the quarter ending March 31, 2022. The high end was below $93,728,900, or 95% of the prior-year quarter’s $98,662,000. The earliest public date remains unresolved because I could verify the announcements for two January management webcasts but could not verify the remarks delivered at either event.

coverage.detail: November 22, 2021, Q4 FY2021 release. Cerence guided revenue to $91 million–$96 million for the December 2021 quarter and $400 million–$425 million for FY2022. Neither range specifies revenue for the March 2022 quarter.
December 15, 2021, CEO transition release. Cerence reaffirmed the November range specifically for fiscal Q1, the quarter ending December 31.
January 6 announcement for the January 11 Needham fireside chat with the CEO and CFO. It gives the webcast details without a revenue forecast. I could not verify a replay or transcript.
January 19 announcement for the January 25 Baird fireside chat with the CEO and CFO. It gives the webcast details without a revenue forecast. I could not verify a replay or transcript.

February 7, 2022, Q1 FY2022 release. The outlook explicitly identifies the quarter ending March 31. The Q2 2022 GAAP revenue row shows a low of 82,000 and a high of 86,000, in thousands of dollars. The same release gives Q2 FY2021 GAAP revenue of 98,662 in the same units.
February 7 earnings-call presentation, Exhibit 99.2. The Q2 FY2022 guidance slide compares the $82 million–$86 million forecast directly with Q2 FY2021 revenue of $98.7 million, rounded.

May 6, 2022, preliminary results issued with the leadership announcement. Cerence narrowed the fiscal Q2 estimate to $85.5 million–$86.5 million and identified February 7 as the date it had given the $82 million–$86 million range.

May 10, 2022, actual results. The consolidated statements report total revenue of $86,280,000 versus $98,662,000 for the three months ended March 31, 2022 and 2021. The GAAP revenue reconciliation independently gives the same amounts.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Cerence’s investor-relations archive timestamps its Q1 results release February 7, 2022 at 7:30 a.m. EST. Exhibit 99.1 carries the same dateline. This verifies publication of the $86 million upper bound that morning. https://investors.cerence.com/news-events/press-releases?page=17

independent_review.basis: Cerence’s August 8 earnings release explicitly forecast consolidated revenue of $44 million to $50 million for the fiscal quarter ending September 30, 2024. The $50,000,000 high end was below $76,725,800, the threshold calculated as 95% of reported Q4 FY2023 GAAP revenue of $80,764,000.

coverage.detail: May 9 Q2 release. Cerence reported first-half revenue of $206.160 million and forecast $66–72 million for Q3 and $318–332 million for FY2024. Those figures implied a maximum Q4 residual of $59.840 million ($332 million less $206.160 million less $66 million). The release gave explicit ranges only for Q3 and the full year.
May 9 earnings-call remarks also scoped management’s guidance to Q3 and FY2024. The $238 million figure discussed on the call was an annual midpoint excluding legacy-contract revenue.

The issuer’s calendar lists May 21 and June 6 investor conferences between the May and August earnings calls. A search of public conference remarks and presentations found no earlier explicit Q4 consolidated revenue ceiling.
August 8 Q3 presentation. The Q4 FY2024 guidance columns show revenue of $44 million low and $50 million high. Separate columns show revised full-year revenue of $321–327 million.
October 7 CEO appointment release reaffirmed the $44–50 million Q4 revenue range and expressly identified August 8 as the date Cerence had announced it.

November 21 actuals. The consolidated statements give total revenue of $54,805,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2024 and $80,764,000 for the corresponding 2023 quarter. Actual revenue exceeded guidance but remained below the $76,725,800 threshold. Both figures use the reported GAAP perimeter, retaining prior-year legacy-contract revenue.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Cerence’s investor-relations copy says “Released August 8, 2024.” The SEC exhibit carries the same dateline and includes the September-quarter forecast. https://investors.cerence.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/122/cerence-announces-third-quarter-fiscal-year-2024-results

independent_review.basis: Cerence’s May 7 earnings release forecast total revenue of $52 million to $56 million for the fiscal quarter ending June 30, 2025 (Q3 FY2025). The explicit $56 million upper bound was below $67,012,050, the threshold of 95% of the prior-year quarter’s reported GAAP revenue of $70,539,000.

coverage.detail: The February 6 Q1 release gave GAAP revenue guidance of $74 million to $77 million for Q2 ending March 31 and $236 million to $247 million for FY2025. Neither range supplied a June-quarter upper bound.
The February 6 earnings presentation also confined its revenue guidance to Q2 and FY2025. The $20 million of expected fixed contracts applied to Q2.
The issuer’s release archive from the February earnings announcement through early April showed product, board and award announcements. No June-quarter revenue forecast was identified.
The April 16 notice scheduled Q2 results. The archive identifies the May 7 earnings release as the next financial results announcement and timestamps it at 4:05 p.m. EDT.

The May 7 EX-99.1 explicitly gives the June-quarter range as $52 million to $56 million. Management’s expectation of no material fixed-license signings was an assumption underlying the total revenue forecast.
The issuer lists its February 6 and May 7 earnings calls with no intervening investor event. The May 29 TD Cowen and June 10 Evercore conference appearances both followed the qualifying release.
The July 23 notice scheduled the June-quarter results for August 6 and supplied no preliminary revenue figure.

The August 6 release’s consolidated statements show total revenue of $62,236,000 for the three months ended June 30, 2025 and $70,539,000 for the corresponding 2024 quarter. The release labels both amounts GAAP revenue. Actual revenue exceeded guidance and still declined 11.8% year over year.
The August 6 earnings presentation independently confirms the scope of the May forecast. Its Q3 FY2025 results slide compares total revenue against guidance of $52 million to $56 million.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Cerence’s IR press-release archive timestamps the Q2 results release May 7, 2025 at 4:05 p.m. EDT. The same-day Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 contains the explicit June-quarter revenue range.

independent_review.basis: Cerence’s Q1 FY2026 earnings release forecast consolidated revenue of $58 million to $62 million for the fiscal quarter ending March 31, 2026. The $62,000,000 upper bound was below $74,109,500, which is 95% of the $78,010,000 reported for Q2 FY2025. The May results subsequently confirmed the decline.

coverage.detail: November 19, 2025, preceding earnings cycle. Cerence guided to $110 million–$120 million for the December quarter and $300 million–$320 million for FY2026. Neither range established a March-quarter ceiling. The November earnings call likewise gave no explicit Q2 revenue upper bound.
December 8, Raymond James conference. The CFO discussed the $310 million FY2026 revenue midpoint. The public remarks contained no explicit March-quarter revenue ceiling.
January 13, Needham conference. Management reiterated $110 million–$120 million for Q1 and $300 million–$320 million for FY2026. It gave no explicit March-quarter revenue range.

February 4, Q1 earnings presentation furnished as Exhibit 99.2. The Q2 FY2026 guidance table confirms revenue of $58 million low and $62 million high, separately from annual guidance. The quarterly outlook includes the expected fixed-license revenue.
March 16, interim conference notice. Cerence announced CFO one-on-one meetings for March 23 and gave no updated revenue figure.

The issuer’s dated release archive covers the interval from February 4 through May 7. The April 27 announcement scheduled Q2 results for May 7. The search found no intervening public preliminary results or revised Q2 revenue range.

May 7, actual results. The consolidated table reports GAAP revenue of $64,192,000 and $78,010,000 for the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. Actual revenue exceeded the February guidance ceiling but remained below the $74,109,500 cutoff.

independent_review.publication_date_evidence: Cerence’s press-release archive timestamps the Q1 FY2026 release at February 4, 2026, 4:05 p.m. EST. The release furnished as Exhibit 99.1 carries the same February 4 dateline and explicitly identifies March 31, 2026 as the end of the forecast quarter.
